title: Ephemeral fallback arbiter with connection timeout pacing and temporal-SLO bridge (rollback fix)
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Introduces an ephemeral fallback arbiter that paces connection timeouts and a temporal SLO credit bridge to reduce circuit flapping. Includes rollback safety for tenant limiter behavior. Safe rollout via canary, no user-facing breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: Recent incidents showed oscillation when regional circuits reopened under short-lived load spikes. The tenant limiter combined with aggressive reconnects caused brief throughput collapse in neighboring regions. This PR introduces an ephemeral fallback arbiter that probes candidate fallbacks with paced connection timeouts (connection pacing) and a temporal SLO bridge that grants short-term acceptance credits which decay deterministically. The arbiter reduces noisy reopen attempts and prevents rapid circuit flip-flops while allowing fast failover when capacity is truly available.

Design summary: single continuous description below. The arbiter sits between the routing decision and the fallback commit. Instead of immediately switching traffic to a fallback region/variant, the arbiter issues controlled probe connections with an exponential pacing timelock per candidate (initial delay + jitter + backoff). Probes use a soft connection timeout tuned to avoid long-hanging sockets. Successful probes consume a small temporal credit from a per-tenant SLO bridge; credits are earned on sustained success and decay with a configurable half-life. If enough credits accumulate within a short window, the arbiter performs a controlled failover. If credits decay or probes fail, the arbiter throttles subsequent attempts and escalates to a more conservative fallback (lower capacity variants) or returns an overloaded response to the caller (guided SLO degradation).

Implementation notes: 
- New package: internal/arbiter with two main components: probe_scheduler and slo_bridge (credit ledger).
- Probe scheduler implements connection pacing and timelock, uses region health metrics and short-lived TCP connect+TLS handshake probes to validate candidate nodes.
- SLO bridge implements per-tenant ephemeral credits, deterministic decay (half-life seconds), and a safety cap to avoid amplification.
- Integration with routing: router/decision now calls arbiter.ProbeAndDecide(ctx, candidate_list, tenant_id, policies). Backwards compatible: if arbiter disabled via flags, behavior is unchanged.
- Rollback fix: previous tenant limiter change (feature/tenant-limiter-warmup) introduced a fast-path that allowed bursts which can interact badly with immediate fallback. This PR reverts that fast-path for mainline and introduces a gated warmup only for Dedicated pools behind feature gate.

Checklist: 
- [x] unit tests for slo_bridge (decay semantics, cap enforcement)
- [x] unit tests for probe_scheduler (pacing backoff, timeout)
- [x] integration test that simulates regional reopen flapping
- [x] CI passing on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
- [x] canary rollout plan added to docs/ops/fallback-arbiter.md
- [x] observability: added metrics (arbiter.probes_total, arbiter.credits, arbiter.failover_attempts) and traces for probe lifecycle

Testing and rollout: 
- Local integration with the benchmark-lab harness reproduced a previous incident sequence and verified that the arbiter prevented cascade failures.
- Canary rollout: 2% traffic in us-west initially for 24h, then 10% for 6h, then 100%. Health checks and SLO regressions monitored; automatic rollback on latency >10% or error-rate >0.5% relative to baseline.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: probe load could add overhead. Mitigation: probes are short-lived, capped per region, and scheduled with backoff; metrics included to watch probe cost.
- Risk: incorrect decay parameters could delay legitimate failovers. Mitigation: conservative defaults and feature flags to tune half-life and credit thresholds at runtime.

Related work: ties to ENG-2182 (failover stability initiative) and SRE-501 incident postmortem.

review_comments: Evan Brooks: Nice design. Two questions: 1) how do we bound probe concurrency across many tenants? 2) please add an integration simulation for a 3-region reopen scenario.

Maya Singh (author): Answered: probe concurrency is bounded by per-region shared semaphore and per-tenant token; added tests for 3-region scenario in integration test. See commit b2a77e9 and tests/integration/fallback_arbiter_flap_test.go
Lena Morrison: Can we add a metric for average probe latency and a debug flag to force immediate success for chaos testing?

Samir Patel: The tenant limiter revert needs a short note in the changelog to make SRE aware of the behavior change during rollout. Also request to add a telemetry alert for probe-error-rate > 2% sustained over 5m.
Maya Singh (author): Added changelog entry and alert in deploy/monitoring/alerts.yaml; pushed in e7d1a99. Also included runbook steps to reduce probe concurrency if cost observed.
